title: Elastic swarm by marginal gain vs fixed N

hypothesis.statement: An elastic rule that adds agents while the expected marginal gain (ΔP·V) exceeds the marginal cost, with ΔP estimated by a Bayesian model of difficulty, delivers lower cost per accepted task than any fixed N while maintaining the acceptance rate; the optimal size moves from 1 → micro → macro with task difficulty and value, and the rule only works well if the ΔP model accounts for error correlation.

predictions.text: For V in {10, 20}, elastic-seq has lower cost per accepted task than every fixed-N (N=1,3,5,9; disjoint 95% CIs) and an acceptance rate >= that of fixed-3 minus 1 p.p.
For every V in {2,5,10,20,50,100}, the mean net utility of elastic-seq is not significantly lower than that of the best fixed-N (the 95% CI of the paired difference does not lie entirely below 0).
Transitions of the optimal fixed N by class: easy -> 1 for every V>=5; medium -> micro (2..5) for V in [10,50]; coupled -> 0 (do not attempt) for V<=5 and macro (>=6) for V>=50.
A misspecified controller (assumes rho=0) has higher cost per accepted task than the calibrated one for V>=20 (disjoint 95% CIs).
A cheap difficulty probe (cost 0.05, identifies the class correctly 80% of the time) increases net utility relative to elastic-seq for V>=10 (paired 95% CI > 0).
elastic-doubling (batches 1,2,4,8,16) uses fewer mean rounds than elastic-seq, with cost per accepted task at most 20% higher, for V>=10.

params.coupling_note: "coupled" = low per-attempt success chance and high correlation between attempts (interdependent bugs); decomposition/specialisation NOT modelled
params.utility: U = V*[accepted and correct] - cost - V*[accepted and wrong]  (a false accept costs as much as the value)

policies.fixed-N: N attempts in parallel, all tested; delivers the 1st that passes; 1 round
policies.elastic-seq: one attempt at a time; before each attempt computes P(next correct | k failures) from the Bayesian posterior (class, latent factor) and continues if P*V >= cost of attempt+test
policies.elastic-doubling: like elastic-seq, but in batches 1,2,4,8,16: expands if P(>=1 correct in the batch)*V >= cost of the batch
policies.elastic-mis: elastic-seq with a misspecified model (assumes rho=0 in every class)
policies.elastic-probe: pays for a class probe (cost 0.05, 80% correct) and uses the posterior conditioned on the probe

sensitivity.note: optimal fixed N (exact) for a single isolated class with individual success probability p; "marginal value of the 2nd agent" = U(N=2)-U(N=1)
